subject: Guardian: Assurance slab & renewal credits
messages:
From: Sasha Reed <sasha@guardian.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@guardian.ai
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Guardian: Assurance slab & renewal credits

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concise ask so we can include SLA terms in our scoring. High level: we need (1) uptime tiers for API endpoints (standby / standard / critical), (2) clear crediting calculus for missed targets, and (3) an early-renewal incentive if we commit on a 12‑month contract before our current vendor term expires in Q3.

Can you send a simple proposal that shows: uptime thresholds (e.g., 99.5 / 99.9 / 99.95), corresponding credit % by band, and one or two packaging options (seat vs commit). Also indicate any volume rebate you can offer if we hit a $200k or $500k ARR commit. Our procurement timeline: decision window is late June; PO will be issued by early July if terms align.

Attaching our high-level SOW and the list of endpoints we consider critical.

Attachments: Guardian_SOW_Q2.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Sasha
Sasha Reed
Head of Platform SRE
Guardian Analytics
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sasha Reed <sasha@guardian.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Guardian: Assurance slab & renewal credits

Sasha — thanks for the clear ask, appreciate the timeline.

Summary below and attaching a short SLA grid that maps bands to credits and sample pricing buckets. High-level points:

- Uptime bands (per-month, per-app):
  * Bronze: 99.5% — 5% credit of monthly service fees
  * Silver: 99.9% — 10% credit
  * Gold: 99.95% — 20% credit

- Packaging options:
  * Commit model (recommended for cost predictability): tiered commit with volume rebates (see attached).
  * Seat/agent model: quoted for smaller pilots, less favorable unit economics at scale.

- Early renewal credit: we can offer a one-time 3% TCV credit if you sign and fully commit 60+ days before your current vendor term ends. If we need a stronger incentive we can convert part of that into a service credit applied across Q1 of the contract.

- Escalation coverage: Priority lane (Gold) includes 24/7 escalation on-call with 1-hour initial response SLA; Silver: business-hours with 4-hour response; Bronze: standard 8x5.

- Volume rebates: preliminary guide — 5% rebate after $200k committed ARR, 10% rebate after $500k. Exact structure depends on term and payment cadence.

Would you be open to a 45‑minute call Monday to go through the grid and lock on which endpoints map to Gold vs Silver? If procurement needs a written concession for negotiation we can follow with a PDF quote and a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Attaching: sla-grid.xlsx, rdw-proposal-v1.pdf

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sasha Reed <sasha@guardian.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@guardian.ai
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Guardian: Assurance slab & renewal credits

Dylan — thanks for the fast turn. A few quick clarifications from the procurement side:

1) Baseline: our goal is to make 99.9 the baseline for production (we have multiple consumer-facing models). Can you show a proposal where 99.9 is the default and 99.95 is the premium lane?
2) Credits: procurement prefers dollar-denominated credits for easier rebate accounting (e.g., $X credit per hour of downtime) — can you translate the % model to a per-hour monetary calculation for standard contract values?
3) Burst capacity: we need an explicit clause about burst capacity — guaranteed burst for N hours per month before overage pricing applies.
4) Timeline: our legal team may request a 60‑day review once we submit redlines; we need DocuSign-ready copies to avoid back-and-forth.

If you can get a variant that sets 99.9 as baseline with the requested dollarized credit figures, we should be able to move to commercial review next week.

On the call items: propose Monday 11am PT.

—Sasha

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sasha Reed <sasha@guardian.ai>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Guardian: Assurance slab & renewal credits

Hi Sasha — looping in formally. Thanks for the detailed points; we can accommodate the three asks with the following commercial positions (subject to final T&Cs):

1) Baseline shift: set 99.9% as baseline (Silver) and 99.95% as Gold. We will reframe credits into a dollar-denominated schedule. Example: for a $120k annual contract, each 1 hour of downtime in the Silver band equals a $1,250 credit (illustrative) — we will produce a table tied to contract value.

2) Burst capacity: we can guarantee 2 hours/month of pre-approved burst at no extra cost in the Gold lane; additional burst hours billed at our published overage rate (we'll include a cap and a 30-day notice carveout for exceptional usage).

3) Early renewal: escalate the early-renewal incentive to a 4% TCV credit if signed 90+ days prior to contract expiry (we can tier at 1.5% for 60+ days as an alternative).

4) Volume rebate: commercial offer — 7% rebate at $200k commit, 12% at $500k (applied as pre-paid credit against invoices).

Next steps:
- We will circulate a revised SLA table with dollarized credits and exact burst wording by EOD tomorrow.
- I'll include a DocuSign-ready addendum tied to deal RDW-2025-4721 for your procurement review.

If that aligns, please confirm the list of endpoints to map to Gold. I recommend we include: inference-api.prod.guardian.ai (high qps), realtime-scorer.guardian.ai, and embeddings-service.guardian.ai as Gold candidates.

Thanks — kim

Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
